segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to EnglishPod.
My name is Marco.
And my name is Catherine.
And today we're going to be visiting one of my favorite places, I must say.
segments.zh: 今天我们将参观我最喜欢的地方之一，我必须说。

segments.en: Really?
So you're a big meat eater?
I am.
I have to have meat every day, so that's why I usually go to the butcher.
segments.zh: 我必须每天吃肉，所以我才经常去肉铺。

segments.en: All right.
So vegetarians be warned, today's dialogue is all about eating meat and where to go to get meat.
segments.zh: 所以素食者要注意，今天的对话就是吃肉和去哪里买肉。

segments.en: So as Marco said, that place is called the butcher's.
segments.zh: 正如马可所说，那个地方叫肉铺。

segments.en: So we're going to be visiting the butcher and we're going to learn all the different types of meat you can find there.
segments.zh: 所以我们要去肉铺，学习你在那里能找到的各种不同的肉类。

segments.en: Great.

So we don't have anything to preview, but before we get started, just like to mention that you're going to hear a lot of different kinds of words and we'll be back in a minute to talk about what they mean.
segments.zh: 所以我们没有任何东西可以预览，但在我们开始之前，只是想提一下你会听到很多不同类型的单词，我们会在一分钟内回来讨论它们的含义。

segments.en: Hi, what can I get for you?
I'd like half pound of ground beef, please.
Good choice.
Our ground beef is extra lean, if you know what I mean.
segments.zh: 我们的牛肉馅脂肪特别少，你懂我的意思吧。

segments.en: Could I also have half a dozen pork chops and two pounds of boneless chicken breast?
segments.zh: 再给我六块猪排和两磅去骨鸡胸肉，好吗？

segments.en: No, no, no chicken breasts at the moment.
But we have some nice chicken thighs.
segments.zh: 不过我们有些很不错的鸡腿肉。

segments.en: No, that won't do.
I'll take this smoked ham you have here.
segments.zh: 那我要这里的烟熏火腿吧。

segments.en: Sorry, is there anything else?
Is this salami and bologna you have here?
segments.zh: 这里的是萨拉米香肠和博洛尼亚香肠吗？

segments.en: Yes, it's very fine meat.
Made it myself.
Sounds good.
Okay, that's it.
Wait, we have T-bone, rib eye and sirloin steaks.
segments.zh: 等等，我们有 T 骨、肋眼和沙朗牛排。

segments.en: They are very fresh.
Just came from the slaughterhouse.
No, that's okay.
Really, I think that's all for today.
segments.zh: 真的，我想这就是今天的全部内容。

segments.en: Okay, that'll be $34.50.
All right, we're back.
So this butcher was kind of creepy in the beginning.
segments.zh: 所以这个屠夫一开始有点令人毛骨悚然。

segments.en: Very creepy in the beginning.
segments.zh: 一开始非常令人毛骨悚然。

segments.en: I think that's usually the conception that you have of butchers because they always have a knife and they're always covered in blood, but it's not human blood.
segments.zh: 我认为这通常是你对屠夫的概念，因为他们总是有一把刀，而且他们总是被血覆盖，但这不是人类的血液。

segments.en: Right, like the movie Sweeney Todd.
segments.zh: 对，就像电影斯威尼托德一样。

segments.en: Did you see that?
Yeah, like Sweeney Todd.
segments.zh: 是的，就像斯威尼托德一样。

segments.en: The butcher of Fleet Street.
But we actually took a look at a lot of different types of meat that the woman was ordering.
segments.zh: 但我们实际上看了那位女士点的很多不同种类的肉。

segments.en: So why don't we take a look at these now in Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不现在在语言要点中看看这些。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
Okay, so the first is a classic cut.
segments.zh: 好吧，第一个是经典的肉类部位。

segments.en: This is something that we had at my house about once a week growing up.
segments.zh: 这是我从小到大在我家大约每周都会吃一次的东西。

segments.en: It's called a pork chop.
Pork chop.
So a pork chop comes from the animal, the pork or pig.
segments.zh: 所以猪排来自动物、猪肉或猪。

segments.en: Yeah, we actually don't say pork to mean the animal.
segments.zh: 是的，我们其实不会用 pork 来指那种动物。

segments.en: Pork just means the kind of meat that comes from a pig.
segments.zh: 猪肉只是指来自猪的那种肉。

segments.en: So big difference there when we're talking about food, we say pork.
segments.zh: 所以这里有很明显的区别，谈到食物时我们说 pork。

segments.en: Oh, wow.
And what about a pork chop?
So what exactly is that?
Chop is usually just on the bone and oftentimes it's fried or baked, I guess, but it's just a piece of pork on the bone and a chop, you just imagine a knife chopping something.
segments.zh: 我猜 chop 通常就是带骨头的，而且常常是油炸或烤制的，但它其实只是带骨的一块猪肉，说到 chop，你只要想象一把刀在剁东西。

segments.en: All right, so a pork chop, very good.
And after pork chops, we were ordering some ground beef.
segments.zh: 在猪排之后，我们点了一些碎牛肉。

segments.en: All right, so ground beef is another important one.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以碎牛肉是另一件重要的事情。

segments.en: Ground beef is beef that's been chopped up and pushed through a machine that kind of pushes it out in very, very small bits and pieces.
segments.zh: 碎牛肉是被切碎并推过一台机器的牛肉，它将其推出非常非常小的碎片。

segments.en: There's no bones.
So ground comes from the verb to grind.
segments.zh: 所以 ground 来自动词 to grind。

segments.en: So to grind up meat, to make it very, very small pieces.
segments.zh: 也就是把肉绞碎，让它变成非常非常小的碎块。

segments.en: Right, so if you want to make a spaghetti bolognese, the kind of beef you use is ground beef or even hamburgers.
segments.zh: 对，所以如果你想做意大利肉酱面，你用的那种牛肉就是碎牛肉，甚至做汉堡也是。

segments.en: Oh, yeah, exactly.
So ground beef, you ground up beef.
segments.zh: 所以碎牛肉，你把牛肉磨碎。

segments.en: What other things would you grind?
You could grind your teeth.
Some people do that when they're sleeping, they grind their teeth.
segments.zh: 有些人在睡觉时会这样做，他们会磨牙。

segments.en: You can grind, you have pepper grinders.
segments.zh: 你可以磨，比如有胡椒研磨器。

segments.en: You know, peppers sometimes come in balls and you have to grind them to make them smaller and broken down.
segments.zh: 你知道，胡椒有时是一颗颗的，你得把它们磨碎、磨细。

segments.en: Very good.
So that's ground beef and from the verb to grind.
segments.zh: 所以这就是碎牛肉，来自动词 to grind。

segments.en: Now we are buying some boneless chicken breasts.
segments.zh: 现在我们要买一些无骨鸡胸肉。

segments.en: All right, so boneless, as you have guessed, means without bones.
segments.zh: 好吧，正如你所猜测的那样，无骨的意思是没有骨头。

segments.en: And chicken breasts are usually just a really nice, juicy, kind of tender cut of meat from the chicken, from the underside of the chicken where obviously, yeah, they have it.
segments.zh: 鸡胸肉通常只是一种非常美味、多汁、嫩嫩的肉块，从鸡肉的下面，显然，是的，他们有它。

segments.en: It's not a wing, it's not a leg, it's just a chicken breast.
segments.zh: 它不是翅膀，不是腿，只是鸡胸肉。

segments.en: All right, so boneless chicken breast.
Now usually it is boneless, right, when you buy it at the supermarket.
segments.zh: 现在通常它是无骨的，对了，当你在超市买的时候。

segments.en: Yeah, yeah.
Next up, we've got some classic deli counter favorites.
segments.zh: 接下来是熟食柜台的几样经典人气食品。

segments.en: These are our cold cuts.
All right, so cold cuts.
Now this means that they are cold?
segments.zh: 现在这意味着他们很冷？

segments.en: Oh, well, yeah, they're cold.
But I think cold cuts, the most important thing to remember here is that they're mostly like kinds of salami or cured meats.
segments.zh: 但我认为冷切，这里最重要的是要记住的是它们大多像香肠或腌肉。

segments.en: So these are salt cured or they're dried meats.
segments.zh: 所以这些是盐腌制的，或者它们是干肉。

segments.en: And you usually have them on sandwiches, so like a salami sandwich.
segments.zh: 你通常把它们放在三明治上，就像意大利腊肠三明治一样。

segments.en: So like cured meat, you mean that meat hasn't been cooked?
segments.zh: 所以就像腌肉一样，你的意思是肉没有煮熟？

segments.en: Oh, no, it's not been cooked, but it's treated in a way that allows it to last for a very long time.
segments.zh: 哦，不，它没有煮熟，但它的处理方式可以让它持续很长时间。

segments.en: So they look like long, long tubes of meat.
segments.zh: 所以它们看起来像长而长的肉管。

segments.en: They look very dry.
They look very dry, like beef jerky, for example.
segments.zh: 例如，它们看起来非常干燥，就像牛肉干。

segments.en: All right, so cured meat.
Now, for example, we have salami and bologna.
segments.zh: 例如，我们有意大利腊肠和博洛尼亚。

segments.en: Bologna.
Now, it's interesting because bologna is actually spelled B-O-L-O-G-N-A.
segments.zh: 现在，这很有趣，因为博洛尼亚实际上拼写为 B-O-L-O-G-N-A。

segments.en: So you would say bologna or something like that.
segments.zh: 所以你会说博洛尼亚或类似的东西。

segments.en: Well, I think it comes from the Italian bologna.
segments.zh: 嗯，我认为它来自意大利博洛尼亚。

segments.en: But it's definitely a change that happened in the English language when it came over from Italy.
segments.zh: 但这绝对是当它来自意大利时在英语中发生的变化。

segments.en: But bologna is a kind of meat that's got a very funny looking name.
segments.zh: 但 bologna 是一种肉，它的名字看起来很有趣。

segments.en: Yeah, see, you're more sophisticated than I am.
That's why you know this difference.
segments.zh: 这就是为什么你知道这种区别。

segments.en: I just speak Italian.
All right, so you have salami, bologna, and...
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你有意大利腊肠、博洛尼亚和...

segments.en: Pastrami.
Pastrami.
What about ham?
Is that considered a cold cut?
You can have ham in the cold cut section because ham sometimes comes in tubes that you slice.
segments.zh: 火腿也可以放在冷切区，因为火腿有时是装成一条条、由你来切片的。

segments.en: But ham is also just a normal kind of pork.
segments.zh: 但火腿也只是一种普通的猪肉。

segments.en: But ham is cured, you know.
segments.zh: 但火腿是腌制过的，你知道。

segments.en: Like a smoked ham.
Exactly.
Or smoked turkey, one of my favorites.
segments.zh: 或者烟熏火鸡，我的最爱之一。

segments.en: Very good.
And, well, now moving on from the cold cuts, we're going to concentrate on steaks.
segments.zh: 而且，好吧，现在从冷盘中继续前进，我们将专注于牛排。

segments.en: Ooh, steaks.
So there are a thousand kinds of steaks in this world and every city seems to have its own kind.
segments.zh: 所以这个世界上有一千种牛排，每个城市似乎都有自己的种类。

segments.en: But here we're only looking at three, the first of which is the T-bone.
segments.zh: 但在这里我们只看三个，其中第一个是 T 骨。

segments.en: All right, the T-bone steak, I think, is one of the most popular ones.
segments.zh: 好吧，我认为 T 骨牛排是最受欢迎的牛排之一。

segments.en: Definitely.
It's a steak that's pretty big, right?
segments.zh: 这是一块相当大的牛排，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, well, yeah, it can be.
And it has a bone inside that looks like a T.
segments.zh: 它里面有一块看起来像T的骨头。

segments.en: All right, so you're saying, Marco, that the T-bone is named after the shape and the look of this steak.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你是说，Marco，T 骨是以这种牛排的形状和外观命名的。

segments.en: Yeah, T-bone steak.
All right.
And as well as our next one is also a rib eye.
segments.zh: 以及我们的下一个也是肋眼。

segments.en: Okay, so the rib eye, I think, actually has a piece of the rib in it.
segments.zh: 好吧，我想，肋眼实际上有一块肋骨。

segments.en: So the rib is the bone and there's a circle, which is kind of a, it's, it's a, the piece of meat is sliced off the rib and the circle is actually part of that rib.
segments.zh: 所以肋骨就是那块骨头，上面有一个圆圈，这块肉是从肋骨上切下来的，那个圆圈其实就是肋骨的一部分。

segments.en: So there's a little bit of bone in it.
But it's not as bony as the T-bone.
segments.zh: 但它不像 T 骨那样骨头多。

segments.en: Right.
So it does have one small bone that kind of looks like an eye because you can see through it.
segments.zh: 所以它确实有一根看起来像眼睛的小骨头，因为你可以看穿它。

segments.en: And our next steak has no bone and is the most tender and the best steak you can have, sirloin steak.
segments.zh: 我们的下一块牛排没有骨头，是你能吃的最嫩和最好的牛排，沙朗牛排。

segments.en: So I think the, the sirloin is definitely the most expensive if you're in a restaurant.
segments.zh: 所以我认为，如果在餐厅里，沙朗牛排绝对是最贵的。

segments.en: Definitely the most tender, I think, of all those.
segments.zh: 我认为，在所有这些中，它绝对是最嫩的。

segments.en: It's delicious.
And usually you can have like a big sirloin steak, like a half a kilo, like a 400 gram sirloin steak.
segments.zh: 通常你可以吃像一块大沙朗牛排，像半公斤，像400克的沙朗牛排。

segments.en: I had a friend who ate a full kilo.
segments.zh: 我有一个朋友吃了整整一公斤。

segments.en: Really?
Sirloin steak.
Wow.
Is there a competition or?
No, there's a kind of steak called la bistecca alla fiorentina in Italy.
segments.zh: 不，意大利有一种叫做 La Bistecca Alla Fiorentina 的牛排。

segments.en: It's the Florentine beef steak and it is, it can be about a kilo of meat.
segments.zh: 这是佛罗伦萨牛排，它可以是一公斤肉。

segments.en: Wow.
Yeah.
I bet you can't even move after that.
segments.zh: 我敢打赌，在那之后你甚至不能移动。

segments.en: No, you're, no, you fall asleep with your head in your soup on the table.
segments.zh: 不，你会，不，你会把头埋在桌上的汤里睡着。

segments.en: All right.
So that's all the meat related words that we have for you today.
segments.zh: 这就是我们今天为您准备的所有与肉类相关的词。

segments.en: So why don't we move on now to Fluency Builder where we're going to take a look at some of the phrases in this dialogue.
segments.zh: 那么，我们为什么不现在继续讨论流利表达，我们将在其中查看此对话中的一些短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
We're going to look at the phrases if you know what I mean.
segments.zh: 我们要看的短语是 if you know what I mean。

segments.en: If you know what I mean.
Now I love this phrase, if you know what I mean.
segments.zh: 现在我喜欢这句话，如果你明白我的意思的话。

segments.en: I do know what you mean.
Well, it's weird.
I like it too.
So you can use it for sarcasm.
segments.zh: 所以你可以用它来讽刺。

segments.en: Yeah.
Right.
Or you can use it to kind of insinuate something.
segments.zh: 或者你可以用它来暗示一些东西。

segments.en: Right.
Exactly.
Yeah.
So here's what you're saying.
You're saying there's a double meaning in what I want to say.
segments.zh: 你是说我想说的话有双重含义。

segments.en: So there's two things I could say and I'm not going to say it outright, but you know, this thing that we can't really say.
segments.zh: 所以有两件事我可以说，我不会直截了当地说，但你知道，这件事我们真的不能说。

segments.en: So for example, we can say she likes to go out if you know what I mean.
segments.zh: 例如，如果你知道我的意思，我们可以说她喜欢出去。

segments.en: All right.
So you're insinuating that not only does she like to go out, but maybe, maybe she goes out a lot, a lot, or maybe she gets drunk or something like that.
segments.zh: 所以你在暗示她不仅喜欢出去，而且也许，也许她经常出去，很多，或者她喝醉了或类似的东西。

segments.en: Yeah.
So it's kind of like a double meaning, but you're trying to be subtle.
segments.zh: 所以这有点像双重含义，但你试图说得隐晦一点。

segments.en: Yeah.
But it's not so subtle because you're actually saying like, this is not what I mean.
segments.zh: 但这并不是那么隐晦，因为你实际上是在说，这不是我的意思。

segments.en: Or she's eating for two if you know what I mean.
segments.zh: 或者如果你知道我的意思，她一个人吃两个人的份。

segments.en: There we go.
So you're insinuating that, well, you're not really insinuating, you're telling me that.
segments.zh: 所以你在暗示这一点，好吧，你不是真的在暗示，你是在告诉我。

segments.en: She's pregnant.
Eating for two is a common idiom in English that means that a person, a woman has a, well, is going to have a baby.
segments.zh: Eat for two 是英语中的一个常见习语，意思是某人，一个女人，嗯，要生孩子了。

segments.en: So here I'm saying, hey, do you know this idiom?
segments.zh: 所以我在这里说，嘿，你知道这个习语吗？

segments.en: She's eating for two if you know what I mean.
segments.zh: 如果你明白我的意思，她一个人吃两个人的份。

segments.en: Right.
Wink, wink, wink.
Wink, wink.
So now why don't we take a look at some other examples of how we could use if you know what I mean in different circumstances when you're trying to insinuate something.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们来看几个其他例子，看看在试图暗示某些事情时，不同场合该怎么用 if you know what I mean。

segments.en: Example one.
She's eating for two now, if you know what I mean.
segments.zh: 如果你明白我的意思，她现在一个人吃两个人的份。

segments.en: Example two.
Tim hit a home run today, if you know what I mean.
segments.zh: 如果你明白我的意思，蒂姆今天打出了本垒打。

segments.en: Example three.
Jim and Laura are going their separate ways, if you know what I mean.
segments.zh: 如果你明白我的意思，吉姆和劳拉正在分道扬镳。

segments.en: All right.
We're back.
So now that that's clear, why don't we move on to our next phrase?
segments.zh: 既然这很清楚，我们为什么不继续我们的下一个短语呢？

segments.en: So this one is a counting phrase.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个计数短语。

segments.en: And for those of you who have heard the word dozen before, it might not be so new.
segments.zh: 对于那些以前听过 dozen 这个词的人来说，它可能不算新鲜。

segments.en: The phrase is half a dozen.
Half a dozen.
So that means half of 12.
So a dozen is 12.
And it's, I'm not really sure when this started being used in English, but a dozen is 12 and half a dozen is then six.
segments.zh: 是的，我不太确定这什么时候开始用英语，但一打是 12，半打是六。

segments.en: Now there's another phrase or another saying that's very common, a dime a dozen.
segments.zh: 还有一个很常见的短语或说法，a dime a dozen。

segments.en: He's a dime a dozen.
So that means you can get 12 of the same type of guys for 10 cents.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着你可以花 10 美分得到 12 个相同类型的人。

segments.en: Right.
So they're easy to find.
They're easy to find.
Yeah.
The dime a dozen.
All right.
Very good.
And moving on to our last one.
segments.zh: 并继续我们的最后一张。

segments.en: When they were talking, they said something about the meat being lean, extra lean.
segments.zh: 当他们说话时，他们说了一些关于肉瘦的，特别瘦的。

segments.en: Okay.
Lean, this does not mean lean on a door.
This is not like resting on something.
This is actually a kind of way to describe food.
segments.zh: 这实际上是一种描述食物的方式。

segments.en: And so food is lean if it's not got much fat, it's not fatty.
segments.zh: 所以如果食物没有太多脂肪，它是瘦的，它不是脂肪的。

segments.en: Okay.
So if it's lean, it doesn't have much fat.
segments.zh: 所以如果是瘦的话，它就没有多少脂肪了。

segments.en: Exactly.
So I prefer to eat lean meats.
So I often eat birds and poultry.
segments.zh: 所以我经常吃鸟和家禽。

segments.en: So chicken, I like it pretty lean.
And if it's got fat on it, I'll cut the fat off.
segments.zh: 如果上面有脂肪，我会切掉脂肪。

segments.en: Oh, okay.
Like the skin.
The skin is fat, right?
Yeah.
All right.
So you can have lean beef.
It doesn't have much fat around it.
Yeah.
And in America actually on the packages at the supermarket, it often says the percentage of meat that you have.
